decisions.reason: As a close extension of the established finishing portfolio with its own product page and no clear negative market signal, we would continue it because the investment is already made and the result can still be seen as unfolding in the market.

Despite being more distant from the core range, the public homepage launch and Germany premiere create a visible commitment that management would be reluctant to reverse so soon, especially since it still supports higher-value print enhancement workflows.

Because it builds directly on the firm's established offer and automation direction, and there is no evidence of failure, management would persist with the product rather than write off the development and launch effort after only one year.

The B2-format multifinisher was prominently announced on the homepage and fits the stated move toward more automated, digitally oriented finishing, so escalation of commitment makes continuation the likely choice.

This hybrid saddle stitcher is close to the core business and supports the firm's broad postpress system logic, so management would keep it given the sunk costs and absence of clearly disappointing results.
The folding add-on unit is closely tied to the installed base and already has a cited customer application, which gives management enough justification to continue rather than exit the product early.
